problem: Visual navigation agents need their own location and heading; prior work assumes ground-truth pose, integrates odometry (accumulating error), or uses CNN/RNN features with no inductive bias for localization.
motivation: Self-localization is crucial for navigation and long-term planning. Slow feature analysis (SFA), from computational neuroscience, is known to extract place- and head-direction-like features from visual streams without integration, so it could give interpretable pose representations for RL.
key_idea: Pre-train a hierarchical slow feature analysis (hSFA) feature extractor on random-walk images so its 32-d representation encodes location and heading, then use it as input for a PPO navigation agent.
insight: The slowness objective, not the architecture, yields location/heading information: a CNN with the same layout as hSFA (CustomCNN) trained via RL performs worse (StarMazeArm 652 vs 69 episode length). hSFA excels when pose is what matters (StarMaze), but it fails under visual symmetries (WallGap) and loses target cues (FourColoredRooms), where PCA/NatureCNN do better because they retain visual cues.
method: hSFA extractor: layers of linear SFA -> quadratic expansion -> Gaussian noise (train only) -> linear SFA -> clipping to [-4,4], applied on receptive fields with strides (10x10/5, 3x3/(2,3)) plus a final fully connected quadratic SFA layer, outputting 32 features
Training of hSFA: layer-wise closed-form solution (whitening, temporal differences, PCA) on 80,000 random-policy frames from target-free environments, pre-trained once per layout, frozen during RL
PPO agent: Stable Baselines3 PPO with an MLP policy (two 64-unit layers) on the frozen 32-d features; 1M steps on StarMazeArm and 2M on the others; 5 seeds
Baselines: NatureCNN (end-to-end), CustomCNN (hSFA-like architecture trained end-to-end), and PCA (32 components, pre-trained on the same data); random and human-optimal reference policies
Representation analysis: top-view feature maps for the first 6 features; heading reconstructed by linear regression to sin/cos from the 32 features (trained on 40k points, tested on 40k points)

setting.backbone: hierarchical SFA (pre-trained, unsupervised) + PPO MLP policy; baselines are NatureCNN, CustomCNN and PCA
setting.training_data: 80,000 random-policy frames per environment layout for hSFA/PCA; PPO trained 1-2M steps in Miniworld
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: turn left pi/12, turn right pi/12, move forward a small step
setting.simulator: Miniworld (custom environments: StarMazeArm, StarMazeRandom, WallGap, FourColoredRooms)
setting.privileged: none at test time (the hSFA pretraining data comes from target-free empty environments)

numbers.extra: average episode length (lower is better), max 1500; mean of 5 seeds, min-max (52, 82); optimal 36, random 1134
average episode length (lower is better), max 1500; range (92, 227); optimal 16, random 1073
average episode length, max 300; range (184, 300); optimal 76, random 300; PCA best at 179
average episode length, max 250; range (225, 239); optimal 53, random 231; NatureCNN best at 187

numbers_note: Custom Miniworld environments, not standard benchmarks; the metric is average episode length (lower is better) at the end of training.
results: hSFA agents are far better on StarMaze (69 vs 415 for NatureCNN on StarMazeArm; 147 vs 309 on StarMazeRandom). They are not better on WallGap (277; PCA 179) or FourColoredRooms (232; NatureCNN 187), where none of the agents does well. Heading is reconstructed from hSFA features to within a few degrees.
limitations: Uses only the current observation with no memory or context; cannot resolve visual symmetries (WallGap) and ignores the target in FourColoredRooms
Layer-wise, non-gradient training is slow, and RL is about half as fast as with a CNN
Needs pre-collected data covering all locations and headings; cannot learn online. Only simple simulated environments and no comparison to state-of-the-art navigation agents
